messages:
alex: FYI I ran a long nsys capture on the 8k-seqlen repro on rtx7. seeing sustained HBM writes and lots of tiny DMA transfers during the KV window. perfetto link below.

mira: can you pull the worst 200ms slice and paste it here? is it the attention path or memcopies?

alex: attention kernels are OK for the prefix, but after ~step 5900 we hit a pattern of many small memcpyAsyncs to KV slots. nsys shows a generic GEMM fallback and memcpy dominating. nvprof excerpt: 
```
0.45%  matmul_opt_fp32   1.4ms  14 GB/s
73.9%  memcpy_htod_sync  29.1ms  660 GB/s
25.65% memcpy_dtoh_async 10.1ms  110 GB/s
```

jon: ugh that sync memcpy is the culprit. batcher config for this run?

alex: dynamic-batcher, max_tokens_per_batch=4096, latency target ~120ms. we were doing micro-sharding near tail which increased distinct KV offsets per step.

cheng: sounds like non-coalesced writes into the HBM KV arena -> L2 and TLB pressure -> DMA storms. quick ideas: coalesce nearby writes in the batcher and prefer fused vectorized KV-copy kernel. also inspect page granularity touched per request.

mira: checked kernel selection logs. runtime flips to safe fp32 kernels when workspace drops below threshold or when seq jumps unexpectedly. config snippet: 
```
model_variant: v1.2
kernel_policy: auto
workspace_bytes: 1.2GiB
allow_quantized: true
```
 sudden seqlen growth tripped the safe-path, removing our optimized fused copy.

alex: example memcpy offsets in the trace look like small unaligned strides (~3KB): 
```
step 1023: memcpyAsync(dst+0x1a4, src+0x5f2, 4096)
step 1024: memcpyAsync(dst+0x2b7, src+0x607, 4096)
```
Not aligned to 128B so vectorized memops can't be used.

jon: are our KV offsets 64-bit? could be alignment/packing bug forcing per-chunk copies.

alex: yes 64-bit offsets. no overflow. but the batcher creates many small copy requests because of micro-batch interleaving.

cheng: actionable plan: 
- add a coalescing pass in batcher to merge contiguous KV writes within a 64KB sliding window
- add runtime flag `--force-kernel=fused_kv_copy` for validation runs
- add a regression perf test that simulates long-seqlen micro-batched traffic (8k+ with jitter)

mira: also request Console metrics: per-step HBM write vs read breakdown and cardinality of distinct KV pages touched per request. that will make regressions obvious.

alex: I forced fused_kv_copy locally and re-ran the same trace: HBM peak ~420 GB/s (down from ~680), memcpy ratio dropped, and p95 latency improved. quick numbers: 
```
before: p95=310ms, hbm_peak=680GB/s, memcpy% = 76
after:  p95=130ms, hbm_peak=420GB/s, memcpy% = 18\```

jon: good improvement. we need to validate correctness across batching edge cases though.

cheng: I'll open a PR for the coalescer + a targeted test harness. tagging infra for cluster-wide perf runs across different HBM topologies.

infra-ci: queued a perf job: perf-cluster-large-hbm/1779601234-run. ETA ~6h. will post nvprof and flamegraphs when done.

trace-bot: perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1779601234 | nsys session: https://ci.redwood.internal/nsys/1779601234

mira: please add the trace slices and the perf logs to the runbook under eng-runtime/kvcache. saves time next incident.

alex: added perfetto + nsys to the runbook and the PR description. thanks :thumbsup:
